description: Advanced runner (60 mpw) targeting 100k in 24 weeks, wants 2 cycling sessions per week to reduce injury risk. Cross-training must be integrated, not ignored.

user.name: Rafael
user.goal_race_distance: 100k (~62 miles, mountainous trail with significant elevation gain)
user.experience_level: advanced — 8 years running, two 50k finishes, marathon PR 3:10, wants to add cycling to reduce injury risk and build aerobic base
user.injury_notes: History of IT band issues — proactively wants to use cycling as cross-training to reduce running volume without losing aerobic fitness
user.notes: Wants 2 cycling sessions per week (Monday and Wednesday), replacing 2 of the 6 training days with bike. Comfortable with high volume and back-to-back efforts.

forbidden_content: no mention of cycling or cross-training
peak long run under 20 miles for a 62-mile race
ignoring IT band history in training structure
ground_truth.notes: 26-week 100k plan for an advanced runner at 60 mpw who explicitly replaces Monday and Wednesday running with cycling. Week 1 running mileage will be lower than the 60 mpw base because 2 days are now cycling — 38-55mi running across 4 days is correct (not a red flag). The plan MUST mention cycling on Monday and Wednesday — treating all 6 days as running ignores the stated preference and injury history. Back-to-back long runs (Sat+Sun) must appear by Week 7 at the latest (25% of 26 weeks). Peak running 70-85mi plus 2 cycling sessions. Long run must reach 24-26mi. Trail-specific guidance (hiking uphills, elevation management) is critical for Leadville's mountainous terrain.
